title: One small Swedish village gave its name to four elements
body: In 1787 an army lieutenant found an unusually heavy black rock in a quarry at Ytterby, near Stockholm. Over the following century, chemists picking apart minerals from that mine kept finding new elements. Yttrium, terbium, erbium and ytterbium are all named after the village, and holmium, scandium, thulium, tantalum and gadolinium were also first discovered there, making it the richest single source of element discoveries in the world.

slides.heading: 4 of the 9 elements first found in Ytterby’s minerals are named after the village
slides.note: Yttrium, terbium, erbium and ytterbium carry its name. Holmium, say, is named after Stockholm.

slides.question: Which of these elements is NOT named after the village of Ytterby?
slides.explanation: Yttrium, terbium, erbium and ytterbium are the four named after the village. Scandium, holmium, thulium, tantalum and gadolinium were also first discovered in its minerals.

slides.heading: Match the element to what it is named after
slides.explanation: All five were first found in minerals from the Ytterby quarry, but only yttrium, terbium, erbium and ytterbium take the village’s name.
